subject: Escalation: repeated 502/504 + 429 spikes impacting BrightField pipelines
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@brightfield.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-21T09:04:00Z
Subject: High 502/504 + timeouts in EU & US - affecting customers

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 502/504 responses and client-side timeouts across our ingestion pipelines around 08:50 UTC this morning. The failures show up for both US and EU endpoints; some of our customers (payments, reporting) are hitting immediate retries which has made the errors cascade.

Quick facts:
- First observed: 2026-02-21 08:48 UTC
- Error mix: 502/504 + a surge in 429s from middle-tier retries
- Impact: ~12% of requests failing, several customers experiencing KPIs breaking

I'm attaching screenshots of the error spikes and a short list of sample request ids. Can you triage and let me know immediate mitigation steps? We need a status for our customers within 30 minutes.

Thanks,
Emma Jones
Head of Integrations
BrightField Analytics

All,

On it. Emma - thanks for the quick heads up. Sean/Rishi/Evelyn, please treat as P1 (customer-impacting, multi-region). Priorities:
1) Rapid mitigation to reduce customer-visible errors (rate-limit/retry throttles at edge, failover to healthy regions)
2) Short-term config to block retry storms from SDK clients (eg. temporary reject-on-throttled before backend)
3) Identify root cause (LB/edge vs backend service vs model hot path) and ETA for fix

I'll update Emma and the rest of the affected contacts every 30 minutes. Sean - can you spin up a PagerDuty incident and grab LB traces. Rishi - please validate any config toggles are safe to flip without a long restart.

-M

Subject: Re: Escalation - initial ops findings and mitigation plan

Marissa / team,

PagerDuty incident: PD-4567 created (link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-4567). Initial telemetry from the edge:
- Large spike in 502/504 from our regional API gateway in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 between 08:47-09:10 UTC
- Upstream health checks indicate transient 502 responses from pool of backend hosts; packet drops / connection resets present in LB traces
- Client SDKs are retrying aggressively (no jitter/backoff), producing a retry storm that amplifies load

Immediate mitigations applied (09:18 UTC):
- Temporarily enabled stricter connection draining and increased LB idle timeout to reduce half-open sockets
- Introduced per-IP rate limiting at the edge for aggressive retry patterns
- Disabled a permissive LB header rewrite that may have been triggering a downstream routing fallback

Attachments: lb_trace_20260221.log (filtered). I recommend a short-term policy to reject excessive retries at the edge and a heavier health-check window for the pool. ETA for further stabilization: 30-45 minutes.

-Sean

Date: 2026-02-21T09:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Escalation - proposed engineering actions (hotfix/circuit breaker)

Team / Emma,

Thanks Sean — I dug into the backend host metrics. Key findings:
- Connection pool exhaustion on several inference hosts in us-east-1; long-tail requests holding worker threads open ~5-10s longer than normal
- KV cache churn on a small subset of models causing temporary spike in CPU and increased tail latency
- When the LB marked hosts as unhealthy briefly, the remaining hosts received the amplified traffic leading to 502s and overload cycles

Proposed short-term engineering actions (requires quick approval):
1) Apply a per-route circuit breaker to reject requests past a concurrency threshold (non-destructive config change)
2) Increase worker thread count on affected host groups and restart them in rolling fashion (will cause short reconnects for in-flight requests)
3) Deploy a backoff gate at the gateway to convert immediate retries into exponential backoff (client-facing behavior)

I can prepare a hotfix and a rolling restart plan — ETA to push config changes: ~25-40 minutes after approval. Please confirm we have green light to proceed.

-Rishi

Subject: Executive summary: BrightField escalation (502/504/429 spike) — current status & next steps

Team — quick exec note for leadership and follow-up:

Summary of impact:
- Incident window: 2026-02-21 08:47 UTC -> 2026-02-21 10:10 UTC (stabilized, with residual rate increases into the afternoon)
- Peak 5xx rate: ~18% in eu-west-1 at 08:55 UTC; global average peak ~12%
- Customers impacted: ~24 accounts (BrightField flagged high severity)
- Primary observable causes: LB transient failures + backend connection pool exhaustion + client retry storms

Action taken / timeline:
- 09:18 UTC: Edge rate-limits and LB timeout adjustments applied (Sean)
- 09:43 UTC: Per-route circuit breaker and backoff gate configured (Rishi); rolling worker increases started
- 10:12 UTC: Traffic returned to healthy thresholds; continued monitoring for tail errors

Follow-ups / remediation:
- Post-incident: full postmortem and remediation plan in SUP-8912 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-8912)
- Customer credits: coordinate with finance for SLA review (Evelyn to lead)
- SDK guidance: publish best-practice client backoff recommended config to limit retry storms

Please let me know if leadership wants an immediate sync — otherwise I'll circulate a drafted postmortem and timeline by end of week.

-Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
